chunks: It was narrated to me by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar from his father from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Musa ibn Umar from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abi Sa'id al-Qammat from Umar ibn Yazid from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Washing the head with marshmallow (khatmi) is a protection from headache, a release from poverty, and a purification of the head from dryness.

key_terms.الْحَزَاز: Dryness or scurf of the head
key_terms.الْخِطْمِيِّي: Marshmallow plant (Althaea officinalis), used here for its medicinal and purifying properties

ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of washing the head with marshmallow according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith highlights the intersection of physical hygiene and spiritual well-being in Shia tradition, attributing both medicinal and metaphysical benefits to the use of marshmallow root. It reflects the Imams' holistic view of health, where simple natural remedies like *khatmi* are seen as means to alleviate bodily ailments like headaches and dryness while simultaneously serving as a cause for divine relief from poverty (*baraa'ah min al-faqri*).
